set.prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (PBV development requirements, labor standards): for PBV development involving nine or more contract units, owners, contractors and subcontractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages and the PHA must monitor compliance (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153). Applies when HACM PBVs are attached to new construction or rehabilitation of 9 or more contract units; PBVs placed on existing housing, and the USDA-funded farmworker centers, are not covered by this rule.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set true from 24 CFR 983.153(c) at 9 or more PBV contract units for development; the HACM PBV page itself says nothing on labor standards.

reason: 24 CFR 983.153(c) requires Davis-Bacon wages for PBV development of nine or more contract units.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. Labor Code 1720(b) covers public funds and below-market land transfers; 1720(c)(4) exempts affordable housing paid solely from a former redevelopment Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund (HSC 33334.2/33334.3), but it does not name the post-dissolution Housing Asset Fund (HSC 34176), and layered funds would defeat the 'solely' condition. Outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; the FY 2024-25 Housing Successor report has no labor standards language and no DIR determination on housing successor funds was found.

reason: No program rule or DIR determination states whether prevailing wage applies to Housing Asset Fund awards, so it depends on Labor Code 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. The fund is local money, so Labor Code 1720(b) (public funds, and fees paid or waived under 1720(b)(4)) may reach a funded project; 1720(c)(5)(E) exempts only below-market loans where at least 40% of units are restricted to 80% AMI for 20 years, and fee payments fall outside that exemption. Outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; the Council item on Fund 1020 contains no labor standards language and the Resolution 2023-55 policy was not text-readable.

reason: The Fund 1020 materials state no labor standards rule, so coverage depends on Labor Code 1720(b) and 1720(c) project facts.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule. The RFQ (issued January 25, 2024, no deadline) contains no prevailing wage or labor standards clause. Conveying City parcels below fair market value is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(3), but coverage depends on 1720(c) exemptions and on whichever state or federal sources are layered in, each with its own rule.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; the RFQ PDF served at the source_url was read and has no labor standards terms.

reason: The RFQ states no prevailing wage term, and land conveyance alone leaves coverage to Labor Code 1720(b)(3) and 1720(c) project facts.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No single stated rule. Labor Code 1720(c)(5)(C) exempts assistance to a household for rehabilitation of a single-family home, and the HOME (12 or more units) and CDBG (8 or more units) federal thresholds do not reach owner-occupied rehab, but PLHA ADU loans fund new construction that 1720(c)(5)(C) does not clearly cover, so the outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The Atwater Housing Plan has no labor standards language.
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage left unclear; program mixes ADU construction loans, rental assistance and owner rehab with no stated program rule.

reason: The Housing Plan states no labor rule and the ADU loan component is not clearly within a Labor Code 1720(c)(5) exemption.
